content:
I was recently working on formalising some basic properties of (Quillen) exact categories with the long term aim of defining the Q construction. I noticed that exact categories aren't present on mathlib.

Since I plan to work on this casually over the next few months I wanted to ask if this is something that the category theory maintainers consider worth incorporating into mathlib or not? I realise abelian categories are already present so building up the basic theory of exact categories shouldn't be too difficult.

I have already formalized the Q-construction (about three years ago); it is not yet in mathlib though.
A definition of exact categories is at https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/jriou_localization/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ExactCategory/Basic.lean#L84 and the Q-construction is defined at https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/f6d4a520260ffc638dbc10c89d066252453256c9/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ExactCategory/Q.lean#L117

Oh that's great! Is this going to be incorporated into mathlib? In the long term some basic results of Algebraic K theory would be pretty nice to have.

Waldhausen's s construction and "s weak eq to Q" maybe could be an intermediary goal? The proof involving Segal's edgewise subdivision I think is accessible.

I have not thought about further applications, as the basic results about algebraic K-theory rely on Theorem A and B by Quillen, which may reasonably enter mathlib only when we have results about the model category structure on simplicial sets (which I formalized at https://github.com/joelriou/topcat-model-category) and a theory of homotopy (co)limits, bisimplicial sets, etc. (there is a related formalization project of Reedy model category structures at https://github.com/joelriou/reedy).
Otherwise, yes, I intend to upstream my code on exact categories (after some cleaning up, and a slight change of design...).
I see, that sounds pretty good. Formalizing the remaining simplicial homotopy theory would be too complex for me, but I will have a look at your linked repos.
